label: Institution
name: Alternative Democratic Reform Party
summary:
The Alternative Democratic Reform Party (ADR) is a Luxembourgish conservative political party founded in 1987, originally as a pensioners' and retirees' party (CSV, Comité pour la Solidarité des Victimes de la vie) before evolving into a broader right-wing conservative party — representing a strand of conservative politics in Luxembourg, one of the world's wealthiest nations and the heart of European financial infrastructure, where economic liberalism and social conservatism compete with the dominant Christian social and socialist parties.

Luxembourg's political landscape is shaped by its extraordinary wealth (GDP per capita among the world's highest, driven by financial services, steel, and EU institutions) and its unique position as both a founding EU member and host of major EU institutions (European Court of Justice, European Court of Auditors, European Investment Bank). Luxembourg's small population (~660,000) includes a large immigrant component (~47% non-citizen residents) that shapes political debates about identity, welfare, and civic participation.

The ADR has positioned itself on issues of national identity and immigration, opposing the extension of voting rights to non-citizens and advocating Luxembourgish language and cultural identity protection. The party has had limited but consistent electoral presence in Luxembourg's parliament, typically receiving 5-10% of the vote, and represents the conservative-nationalist strand in an otherwise quite internationalist and progressive small nation.
